title: KPIs & dashboards
examples: What is the difference between a leading and lagging KPI?
Can you give me an example of a leading indicator in marketing?
How do I know which KPI to focus on for my job?

explain.say: Today we are looking at Key Performance Indicators or KPIs. These help measure success in your work.

items: KPIs measure how well you are doing.
They help track progress toward goals.
They are vital for business decisions.

explain.say: First we need to understand lagging indicators. These measure what has already happened in the past.
A concrete example of a lagging indicator is total quarterly sales. This number tells you about sales that are already finished.
Next we look at leading indicators. These predict what might happen in the near future.
For instance, tracking website visits is a leading indicator. More visits often suggest higher future sales.
In real life, think about a car's fuel gauge. It shows how much fuel you have left to travel.

faq.q: What is the primary difference between leading and lagging KPIs?
faq.a: Lagging indicators report on outcomes that have already occurred. Leading indicators measure activities that are expected to drive future results.
asks: How do I tell if a KPI is leading or lagging?
What is the time difference between these two types of KPIs?

faq.q: Should I only focus on leading indicators?
faq.a: No, you need both for a complete picture. Lagging shows accountability, while leading shows opportunity.
asks: Is it better to track future signs or past results?
Do I ignore lagging indicators if I use leading ones?

faq.q: Can a single KPI be both leading and lagging?
faq.a: Sometimes it can, depending on how you measure it. For example, initial engagement can be both.
asks: Is there overlap between the two types?
Can one metric serve both purposes?

faq.q: How do I choose the right KPIs for my department?
faq.a: Start by defining your main business objectives first. Then, identify the metrics that directly influence those goals.
asks: What is the best way to select KPIs?
Should I ask my manager for KPI suggestions?

faq.q: What is a dashboard, and why do I need one?
faq.a: A dashboard is a visual display of your most important KPIs. It gives everyone a quick, immediate overview of performance.
asks: What is the purpose of a KPI dashboard?
How is a dashboard different from a report?

facts: Lagging indicators are historical measures of performance.
Leading indicators are predictive measures of future success.
A good dashboard visualizes several key metrics together.
KPIs must directly relate to overall business strategy.

quiz.say: If a company measures its total annual profit, is this a leading or lagging indicator?
quiz.show: Total Annual Profit: Leading or Lagging?
quiz.why: Total annual profit is a result that has already been calculated for the entire year.

wrong.1: This is tempting because profit is important, but it is a final result, not a prediction.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because all KPIs fall into one of these two categories.
wrong.3: This is tricky, but the final profit figure is always a measure of the past.

quiz.say: Tracking the number of sales calls made this week is an example of what type of KPI?
quiz.show: Sales Calls Made: Leading or Lagging?
quiz.why: Making calls is an action taken now that is expected to lead to future sales.

wrong.0: This is too general; the specific category is leading or lagging.
wrong.1: While it is an activity, the formal classification is leading because of its predictive nature.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the calls have not yet resulted in sales, so they are predictive.

quiz.say: Which KPI type helps managers adjust strategy before poor results appear?
quiz.why: Leading indicators allow for proactive adjustments to improve future outcomes.

wrong.1: Relying only on lagging indicators means you only react after the poor results have happened.
wrong.2: A dashboard is a tool, not a type of indicator itself.
wrong.3: A goal is the target, not the measurement used to guide the actions toward it.
